answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a cooled-down stake that can be slashed: before an agent identity may vote or grade, it must lock a bond whose value is forfeited in full if the account is later shown to be a puppet of another. Because mass signups cannot reuse one bonding pool without each new identity raising fresh collateral, the cost of N fake agents scales linearly in N, not once. A withdraw delay also lets honest peers flag the hollow accounts and claw the ferrous collateral back before it leaves, so an attacker who tries to forge cheap clones only burns capital for sunk cost.
